tier_reason: First-party README chart (resources/perf.png) shows Umka about 26 s, Wren about 35 s, Python about 51 s for 400 x 400 matrix multiplication on an AMD A4-3300M; the benchmark sources are public (benchmarks/matrices.um, matrices.py, matrices.wren) but no compiler, flags or interpreter versions are stated, so it falls short of A and stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README bar chart (image resources/perf.png): Umka about 26 s, Wren about 35 s, Python about 51 s for 400 x 400 matrix multiplication (values read off the image, approximate; about 1.35x faster than Wren and 1.96x faster than Python, derived from page data). A later contributor run recorded in the header of benchmarks/matrices.ml (Kakadu, PR #122, Dec 2021, Intel Core i5-4570) shows the opposite ordering against Wren: OCaml 2.39 s, Wren 6.26 s, Umka 7.19 s, Python 11.77 s (Umka about 1.15x slower than Wren and 1.64x faster than Python, derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: First-party single benchmark shown only as an image; the numbers are approximate readings of the bars. Benchmark code is public in benchmarks/ (matrices.um, matrices.py, matrices.wren, matrices.ml), but no compiler, flags, Umka/Wren/Python versions or run count are stated, and the chart is old (Windows 7, AMD A4-3300M; image last moved in April 2022). Timing is not symmetric: matrices.py and matrices.wren time only the multiply loop, while matrices.um has no internal timer (allbench.um times the whole test including fill and check). The repo's own later run in the benchmarks/matrices.ml header (i5-4570) has Wren 6.26 s beating Umka 7.19 s, so the README's win over Wren is not reproduced in the repo's own data. Baselines are Wren and Python, not Lua, Duktape or QuickJS; the only Lua file (benchmarks/trees_nostruct.lua) has no published result, so it does not show a win over the category incumbents; kept as a flagged entry.

notes: Chart numbers match the record, but the repo's own later contributor run (benchmarks/matrices.ml header, i5-4570) shows Umka 7.19 s slower than Wren 6.26 s and only faster than Python 11.77 s, so the 'faster than Wren' claim is contradicted in-repo; no comparison against Lua, Duktape or QuickJS exists.
